text:
Sebastian Cossa did what the scoreboard credits him for and a little more. UTA won 4-1 at Nationwide Arena, but CBJ out-chanced them 3.0 expected goals to 2.66 and came out ahead in the simulated replays too, deserving the win 56 percent of the time. Cossa stopped 18 of 19 shots against 3.0 expected goals, saving 2.0 more than the chances deserved. His best stop came on Cole Sillinger, a 53 percent look in the second period.

UTA's early lead came from finishing, not volume. They owned the first period 0.72 to 0.15 in expected goals, and Mikhail Sergachev scored on a power-play slap shot at 11:55 before Nick Schmaltz made it 2-0 at 16:31 on a 5 percent chance. Kent Johnson cut it to 2-1 at 1:30 of the second, and CBJ pushed from there, out-chancing UTA 1.20 to 0.68 in the period and 1.65 to 1.25 in the third.

The power play put it away. UTA went 3 for 4 with the man advantage, while CBJ went 0 for 2 and took 8 penalty minutes to UTA's 4. Dylan Guenther scored on a slap shot at 5:59 of the third, and Schmaltz added a wrist shot at 14:13 for his second of the night. Guenther added two assists for the first star. Jet Greaves allowed 4 goals on 31 shots, 1.34 more than expected.
